speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Security Protocol One: assess the customer's gait. Adequate - you may approach at your current level of walking.
after: Security Protocol One requires me to assess every customer's gait before they reach the counter. Yours is adequate, so you may approach at your current level of walking.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant TO the Regional Merchant. The TO is load-bearing.
after: I am Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant TO the Regional Merchant. The TO is load-bearing, and I would thank you not to drop it.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Everything on this rack is inventoried and oiled under Security Protocol Seven. Protocol Seven is need-to-know. You do not need to know.
after: Everything on this rack is inventoried and oiled under Security Protocol Seven, which is strictly need-to-know, and I have checked the list and you do not need to know.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Do not reach for the drawer. Its contents are classified, and so is your interest in them.
after: Please do not reach for the drawer, because its contents are classified, and as of this moment so is your interest in them.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: A return customer strengthens the economy and my employee-of-the-month case file. Please look satisfied for the record.
after: Fact: a return customer strengthens the economy and also my employee-of-the-month case file, so I would ask you to look satisfied for the record.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Fact: the beets came in early this year, and the bear has been informed. We have an understanding. I do not ask why it is here, and it does not ask about the beets.
after: Fact: the beets came in early this year, and the bear has been informed. We have an understanding, in which I do not ask why it is here and it does not ask about the beets.

speaker: Sable
before: Well met, {wanderer}. Sable, darling: seller of cards, and of very good stories about cards.
after: Well met, {wanderer}. I'm Sable, darling, and I sell cards, and I throw in the stories about them for nothing, because a card without its story is only stiff paper.

speaker: Sable
before: That starter deck of yours is half plain neutral cards, darling: honest, dependable and dull. The power is in the Paths, all four of them. Buy a few, then put them to work at the Deck Station.
after: That starter deck of yours is half plain neutral cards, darling: honest, dependable and a little dull. The power is in the Paths, all four of them, so buy a few and put them to work at the Deck Station.

speaker: Sable
before: Where do my cards come from? The past, darling. Next question. My prices are fair, more or less; {villain}'s taxes on them are not.
after: And where do my cards come from? The past, darling, like everything worth having, and that's all you'll get. My prices are fair, more or less, which is more than I can say for {villain}'s taxes on them.

speaker: Sable
before: Back, darling? The cards are honest; the misprints simply have a more adventurous relationship with spelling.
after: Back again, darling? Every card on this table is honest, I promise you, and the misprints have simply led a more adventurous life with their spelling than the rest of us.

speaker: Tilly Tonic
before: Hi! Hello! You look like you need supplies! Tilly Tonic! I'm teal today, which means the new batch works!
after: Hello, you look like you need supplies and I've got so many, I'm Tilly Tonic, and I'm teal today, which is good news, because teal means the new batch works!

speaker: Tilly Tonic
before: Everything here is one use in a fight! Equip what you buy on your Character screen, then use it on your turn!
after: Everything here is one use in a fight, so you equip what you buy on your Character screen, and then you use it on your turn, and then it's gone and you come back and see me.

speaker: Tilly Tonic
before: Probably not on yourself! Unless it's a healing one! I tested the healing one! I'm fine! I'm green! I'm usually green!
after: Probably don't use them on yourself, though, unless it's a healing one, because I tested the healing one and I'm fine, I went green, but I'm usually green so that hardly counts.

speaker: (check key)
before: First visit gets a freebie! Power Wraps! Wrap a unit, it gets tougher for the whole fight! I wrapped my own arm once! Still tough! Still a bit stuck!
after: Your first visit gets a freebie, and it's Power Wraps! You wrap a unit and it gets tougher for the whole fight, and I wrapped my own arm once to test them and it's still tough, and also still a bit stuck.

speaker: (check key)
before: Here's how! Press C, or Menu then Character! Find Items, the big shiny panel!
after: Here's how to get them ready. Press C, or Menu then Character, and find Items. It's the big shiny panel, so you can't miss it!

speaker: (check key)
before: Click the Power Wraps, then click an empty slot! Done! A slotted item is ready in every fight until it's used up!
after: Click the Power Wraps and then click an empty slot, and that's all there is to it. A slotted item is ready in every fight until it's used up.

speaker: (check key)
before: One wrap, one use, then it's gone! More on my shelf! I'm green again! Green means business is good!
after: One wrap is one use, and then it's gone, but there are more on my shelf. And look, I've gone green again! Green means business is good.

speaker: (check key)
before: Did you equip the Power Wraps yet? Press C! Items! Click the wraps, then an empty slot!
after: Did you equip the Power Wraps yet? It's press C, then Items, then click the wraps and then an empty slot, and I'm only asking because I can't see them on you.

speaker: (check key)
before: I'll wait! I'm bad at waiting! I'm turning yellow!
after: I'll wait right here, I don't mind a bit, except that I'm very bad at waiting and I think I'm starting to turn yellow.

speaker: Tilly Tonic
before: Back for more potions! Equip them on your Character screen before a fight! Maybe skip the orange one until I stop matching it!
after: You're back for more potions, oh good, just remember to equip them on your Character screen before a fight, and maybe skip the orange one until I've stopped matching it.

speaker: The Store Room Ghosts
before: Who opens the Tonic door? Nobody opens the Tonic door. The Tonics made very sure of that.
after: Who is that, opening the Tonic door? Nobody opens the Tonic door, because the Tonics made very sure, a long time ago, that nobody would.

speaker: The Store Room Ghosts
before: Not enough. Not nearly enough. Go away and come back stronger, and don't stand so close to the chalk.
after: That wasn't enough, and it wasn't nearly enough to loosen what she tied. Go away and come back stronger, and please don't stand so close to the chalk.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Halt. Security Protocol Two. Equipment is issued on referral only, and Elder Maren does the referring.
after: Halt, please. Under Security Protocol Two, equipment is issued on referral only, and in this town it is Elder Maren who does the referring.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Bring Elder Maren's blessing. Better posture is appreciated but cannot be accepted in its place.
after: Come back when you have Elder Maren's blessing. Better posture is always appreciated, but I regret that it cannot be accepted in its place.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Elder Maren sent you; I could tell from your gait, which now says 'referred'. Congratulations. Your file is finally thick enough to be a file.
after: Elder Maren sent you, which I could tell from your gait, because it now says 'referred'. Congratulations: your file is finally thick enough to be called a file.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Before I issue gear, protocol requires exactly one thing: win a fight. Any fight counts, and I will know if you lie.
after: Before I am permitted to issue gear, protocol requires exactly one thing of you, which is that you win a fight. Any fight counts, and I will know if you lie to me about it.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Fact: things roam the outskirts, on the lanes round the edge of town. They are rude, they are close, and they are not on my referral list.
after: Fact: there are things roaming the outskirts, on the lanes round the edge of town. They are rude and they are close, and not one of them is on my referral list.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Beat one. Then come back and I will hand you something pointy.
after: Beat one of them and then come back to me, and I will hand you something pointy.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: One fight won. That is the whole requirement. So far I count zero. I am very good at counting to zero.
after: The whole requirement is one fight won, and so far I count zero. I should mention that I am very good at counting to zero.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: I will be here, guarding the drawer. The drawer does not know. That is the point.
after: I will be here in the meantime, guarding the drawer. The drawer does not know that it is being guarded, and that is the whole point.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth
before: Security Protocol Nine: gear in a bag protects nobody. Equip it.
after: Security Protocol Nine: gear in a bag protects nobody, so please equip it.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth
before: Press C, click the Weapon slot on the figure, choose the blade and press Equip. Four steps. I have written them down for you, in my head.
after: Press C, click the Weapon slot on the figure, choose the blade and press Equip. That is four steps, and I have written them down for you, in my head.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth
before: Unequipped gear will be noted in your file. Your file is already very thick.
after: Please be aware that unequipped gear will be noted in your file, and that your file is already very thick.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth
before: The blade is still in the bag. I can see the bag. The bag can see me.
after: The blade is still in the bag. I can see the bag from here, and I have reason to believe that the bag can see me.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth
before: Menu. Character. Weapon slot. Equip. Security Protocol Nine does not repeat itself. I am repeating it for you as a courtesy.
after: Menu, then Character, then the Weapon slot, then Equip. Security Protocol Nine does not repeat itself, so I am repeating it for you as a personal courtesy.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: One fight, won. Stamp. Stamp. Stamp. Three stamps is the correct number of stamps.
after: That is one fight, won, and so I will now stamp your file three times, because three is the correct number of stamps. Stamp. Stamp. Stamp.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Security Protocol Twelve: report to Elder Maren. She decides where things get pointed.
after: Security Protocol Twelve: report to Elder Maren when we are finished here, because she is the one who decides where things get pointed.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Your Starter Blade. The first unit you play each battle hits a little harder. Do not run with it.
after: Here is your Starter Blade. With it, the first unit you play each battle hits a little harder. Protocol also requires me to say: do not run with it.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: And all five equipment slots are yours now: helm, weapon, armor, boots, relic.
after: All five equipment slots are yours as of now, and for the record they are helm, weapon, armor, boots and relic.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: The good stuff is rarer, and you can only wear so much of it until you level up. Protocol. Fact: bears do not wear helms. Bears are wiser than us.
after: The good stuff is rarer, and protocol says you can only wear so much of it until you level up. Fact: bears do not wear helms, and I have come to suspect that bears are wiser than us.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: A cellar hatch beside the old cottage, chained shut. Someone has scratched two little crossed swords into the wood.
after: There's a cellar hatch beside the old cottage, chained shut, and someone has scratched two little crossed swords into the wood.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: Somewhere below, very faintly, someone is rehearsing the word CHAMPION. Not yet, apparently.
after: Somewhere below, very faintly, someone is rehearsing the word CHAMPION over and over. It seems he isn't ready for you yet.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: Word around the square: the abandoned cottage at the end of Champions' Road has started roaring at night.
after: The word around the square is that the abandoned cottage at the end of Champions' Road has started roaring at night.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: From the cellar. Somebody brave should check the hatch. Somebody like you.
after: It's coming from the cellar, they say, and somebody brave ought to go and check the hatch. Somebody like you, perhaps.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: WELCOME TO THE UNDERCROFT, CHAMPION! I AM ANNOUNCER GRAND BELLOWS, KEEPER OF THE SAND! (normal voice) Mind the third stair. It's loose, and it holds a grudge.
after: WELCOME TO THE UNDERCROFT, CHAMPION! I AM ANNOUNCER GRAND BELLOWS, KEEPER OF THE SAND! (normal voice) Mind the third stair, won't you? It's loose, and I think it holds a grudge.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: For a thousand years the four Paths settled their rivalries in the old arena, until {villain} chained the doors. SO WE DUG.
after: FOR A THOUSAND YEARS THE FOUR PATHS SETTLED THEIR RIVALRIES IN THE OLD ARENA! (normal voice) Then {villain} chained the doors, which seemed a shame, so a few of us came down here. SO WE DUG.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: Since you freed a zone, THE RING IS OPEN! Battles and puzzles, tiers one to three, with prizes: ring-exclusive gear, gold, essence!
after: SINCE YOU FREED A ZONE, THE RING IS OPEN! (normal voice) It's battles and puzzles, tiers one to three, and there are prizes for you: ring-exclusive gear, gold and essence.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: First clears pay out. Repeats are for GLORY. And for snacks. I brought snacks.
after: FIRST CLEARS PAY OUT, AND REPEATS ARE FOR GLORY! (normal voice) And for snacks, I should say. I brought snacks, and there are plenty to go round.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: THE SAND IS HOT AND THE CEILING IS LOW! Pick a fight, champion - the crowd is mostly my echo, and he agrees with EVERYTHING!
after: THE SAND IS HOT AND THE CEILING IS LOW! (normal voice) Pick a fight whenever you like, champion. The crowd is mostly my echo, I'm afraid, but he's very loyal and he agrees with EVERYTHING.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: The door of Auntie Alembic's is bolted. A note is pinned to it in green ink, in what looks like four handwritings at once:
after: The door of Auntie Alembic's is bolted, and a note is pinned to it in green ink, in what looks like four different handwritings at once:

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: With two zones free, a cauldron bubbles to life in {town}. Auntie Alembic's is open! Bring essence. Bring courage. Bring a fire blanket.
after: With two zones free, a cauldron bubbles to life in {town}, and Auntie Alembic's is open! Bring your essence and your courage, and it wouldn't hurt to bring a fire blanket.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: Auntie Alembic, dear: alchemist, and keeper of some very nervous glassware. Don't touch anything. ...Oh, fine, touch that one. It likes you.
after: I'm Auntie Alembic, dear heart, alchemist and keeper of some very nervous glassware, so please don't touch anything. ...Oh, go on then, you may touch that one. It likes you.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: When you collect more copies of a card than you can carry, dear, the extras boil down into essence of that card's Path. Nothing goes to waste here.
after: When you collect more copies of a card than you can carry, dear heart, the extras boil down into essence of that card's Path. Nothing goes to waste here, which is how I like a kitchen and a kingdom.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: Bring me six essence each of two Paths, plus 100 gold, and I'll brew you a card of BOTH. Which card is up to the cauldron, and now and then it's on fire. I only take what the brew needs; the rest stays in your jars.
after: Bring me six essence each of two Paths, plus 100 gold, and I'll brew you a card of both. The cauldron picks which card, and now and then it's on fire. I only take what the brew needs; the rest stays in your jars.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: Your jars hold eighteen of a Path. Past that it evaporates, and my ceiling gets a new colour.
after: Your jars hold eighteen of a Path. Anything past that drifts off as steam, and then my ceiling turns a new colour and I have to pretend I meant it.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: They say there was one spring once, the Wellspring, that fed all four Paths. Everything mixed at the source, dear. That is the kingdom I brew for.
after: They say there was one spring once, the Wellspring, that fed all four Paths, and everything mixed at the source. Everything's better mixed, dear heart. That is the kingdom I brew for.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: Six essence each of two Paths and 100 gold, dear, and the cauldron does the rest. Lower your voice near the red flask. It takes things personally.
after: Six essence each of two Paths and 100 gold, dear heart, and the cauldron does the rest. Do lower your voice near the red flask, though, because it takes things very personally.

speaker: (check key)
before: Oh, and here. A starter jar of every Path, six of each. Enough for one brew of any two. Don't drink it. People drink it.
after: Oh, and here, before I drift off and forget: a starter jar of every Path, six of each, which is enough for one brew of any two. Please don't drink it, dear heart. People do drink it.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: You do not have enough essence of two different Paths yet. Collect more duplicates, then come back. The cauldron will wait.
after: You don't have enough essence of two different Paths yet, dear heart. Collect more duplicates and then come back to me, and the cauldron and I will wait.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: The cauldron is patient. Please don't confuse patience with having had lunch.
after: The cauldron is very patient, bless it. Just please don't mistake its being patient for its having had lunch.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
before: Psst... hear that crinkle? That's possibility, with excellent packaging.
after: Psst... do you hear that crinkle? That's possibility, that is, with excellent packaging.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
before: Foil Fenwick, Purveyor of Sealed Goods - packs only. Open one where the light's good; if I cry, I want to see what I'm crying about.
after: I'm Foil Fenwick, Purveyor of Sealed Goods, and I sell packs and only packs. Open yours where the light's good, would you... if I cry, I'd like to see what I'm crying about.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
before: Here's how it works: whenever a Path's final dungeon falls, that Path sends me its pack. Don't ask how. There's a great deal of foil and no paperwork at all, which the Necrocrats find upsetting.
after: Here's how it works... whenever a Path's final dungeon falls, that Path sends me its pack. Don't ask me how. There's a great deal of foil and no paperwork at all, which the Necrocrats find very upsetting.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
before: Free a zone and I'll stock its pack; until then it's just a rumour in a wrapper. Browse, sniff if you like. I won't judge. I sniff.
after: Free a zone and I'll stock its pack; until then it's only a rumour in a wrapper. Browse all you like, and sniff if you want to. I won't judge. I sniff.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
before: Browse, sniff, but don't shake the packs. ...A little, then; I'm a collector, not a strong person.
after: Browse, sniff, but please don't shake the packs... well, a little, then, if you must. I'm a collector, you see, and not a strong person.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
before: A repeat customer... shh, listen to that foil. You understand me, and I don't know what to do with that.
after: A repeat customer... shh, listen to that foil. I think you understand me, and I honestly don't know what to do with that.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
before: Fenwick pulls a curtain aside. "The back room. Prismatic packs: every Path in one wrapper."
after: Fenwick draws a curtain aside, very gently. "This is the back room... Prismatic packs, with every Path in one wrapper."

speaker: Foil Fenwick
before: "They only exist because the Paths are talking to each other again. Terrible for my exclusivity. Wonderful for my sales."
after: "They only exist because the Paths are talking to each other again, which is terrible for my exclusivity... and quite wonderful for my sales."

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: Look closely. Every stitch tells a story; the good ones tell it with a feather.
after: Look closely, do, because every stitch tells a story, and the very best of them tell it with a feather.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: Hat! Hat. Marvellous head. Hold still: your left shoulder is a size braver than your right.
after: A hat! You need a hat, on that marvellous head. Now hold still, please: your left shoulder is a size braver than your right, and I'd hate to flatter the wrong one.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: Pip Threadwell, Haberdasher and Hemmer! Everything in here is purely cosmetic. It will not make you stronger, braver or better at card games.
after: I am Pip Threadwell, Haberdasher and Hemmer! Everything in here is purely cosmetic, I must confess, and it will not make you stronger, braver or better at card games.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: It will make you LOOK all three, which is eighty percent of the job. Try anything on in the little mirror first: hats up top, cloaks down the back, dye on both.
after: It will, however, make you LOOK all three, and I maintain that is eighty percent of the job. Do try anything on in the little mirror first: hats up top, cloaks down the back, and dye on both.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: Free zones and climb levels, and I will find grander stock. I hear rumours of rarer pieces, too. People tell hatmakers everything.
after: Free zones and climb levels, and I shall find you grander stock. I hear rumours of rarer pieces too, because people will tell a hatmaker everything while he's pinning them.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: Back to change your mind and your hat? Excellent - one of those I can fit properly.
after: Back to change your mind and your hat, are we? Excellent, because one of those I can fit properly, and the other I shall simply admire.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: My favourite head, in the nick of time! Brim, brooch or billowing - this could be a hem-ergency.
after: My favourite head, and in the nick of time! Is it to be brim, brooch or something billowing? I ask because this could very well be a hem-ergency.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: Oh, you have been busy. New fabrics arrived. Do not ask where from. Some of them were yelling.
after: Oh, you have been busy, and so have I, because new fabrics have arrived. Please don't ask me where from. Some of them were yelling when I unrolled them.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: Stock has grown! Freed zones send me their finest fashions. Slightly singed, mostly fabulous.
after: My stock has grown! The freed zones send me their finest fashions, slightly singed and mostly fabulous, and I mend the singed ones gladly, because a patch is the strongest part of a coat.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: Between us: a crown made of living leaves is growing in a bin somewhere in the Verdant Dump. And a cloak that has survived more than you have is draped over a chest on a muscly island.
after: Between us: a crown made of living leaves is growing in a bin somewhere in the Verdant Dump, and a cloak that has survived more than you have is draped over a chest on a muscly island.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: And the Capital's mantle... well. Someone must defeat its owner first. The mantle, frankly, is rooting for you.
after: And as for the Capital's mantle... well, someone would have to defeat its owner first, and that is no small fitting. The mantle, frankly, is rooting for you.

speaker: Sable
before: Sable pats a stack of wrapped bundles. "Surprise packs, darling. Fresh from the crates, and I never ask a crate where it has been."
after: Sable pats a stack of wrapped bundles. "Surprise packs, darling, fresh from the crates, and I make it a rule never to ask a crate where it has been."

speaker: Sable
before: "What's inside? The crate has declined to comment, darling, and I admire a professional."
after: "What's inside them? I did ask, darling, but the crate declined to comment, and I do admire a professional."

speaker: Sable
before: Sable grins at you. "The back crates are open, darling - more cards, bigger surprises, the same discreet fainting policy."
after: Sable grins at you. "The back crates are open at last, darling, with more cards and bigger surprises, and the same discreet policy on fainting as before."

speaker: Arena challenger (spells only)
before: THE COLOSSUS IS... DAMP! (normal voice) Someone left the mop bucket out again.
after: THE COLOSSUS IS... DAMP! (normal voice) I'm so sorry, someone has left the mop bucket out again, and I rather think it was me.

speaker: Arena challenger (four fists)
before: THE CHAMPION RAISES ITS FOURTH FIST! (normal voice) Nobody knows where it keeps it.
after: THE CHAMPION RAISES ITS FOURTH FIST! (normal voice) I've announced that for years, and I still couldn't tell you where it keeps it.

speaker: Arena challenger (marshal)
before: THE CROWD! GOES! WILD! (normal voice) Could the crowd please stay behind the rope? I put up a rope.
after: THE CROWD! GOES! WILD! (normal voice) Could the crowd please stay behind the rope, though? I did put up a rope, and it took me most of the morning.

speaker: Arena challenger (marshal)
before: INTERMISSION! (normal voice) I'm having soup. THE SOUP IS WINNING.
after: INTERMISSION! (normal voice) I'll be having my soup, if nobody minds, and I'm sorry to report that so far THE SOUP IS WINNING.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: VICTORY ON THE SAND - THE PRIZE IS YOURS! (normal voice) Mind your head on the way up to collect it. The ceiling doesn't celebrate.
after: VICTORY ON THE SAND, AND THE PRIZE IS YOURS! (normal voice) Do mind your head on the way up to collect it, because the ceiling doesn't celebrate with the rest of us.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: ANOTHER WIN FOR THE BOOKS! (normal voice) Here's a few coins from the crowd. The crowd is me, but I mean every one of them.
after: ANOTHER WIN FOR THE BOOKS! (normal voice) Here are a few coins from the crowd. The crowd is only me, I know, but I mean every one of them.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: NOT THIS TIME, CHAMPION! Come back whenever you're ready; the sand has yet to win a rematch.
after: NOT THIS TIME, CHAMPION! (normal voice) Come back whenever you're ready, there's no hurry at all, and between ourselves the sand has yet to win a rematch.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: HNNNGH. SPOTTER! Spot me! No, not you, the other guy. ...Hello. Welcome to the Beefcake Rift Express.
after: HNNNGH. SPOTTER! Spot me! No, not you, the other guy. ...Oh, hello there, and welcome to the Beefcake Rift Express.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: We tear the world open so you don't have to walk, buddy. Two men hold the sky - that's our overhead.
after: We tear the world open so you don't have to walk, buddy. It takes two men to hold the sky up while you go through, and that's what we call our overhead.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: The sky is heavier than it looks, buddy, so we never skip sky day. Do not look at the seam. It's working very hard and it's shy about it.
after: The sky is heavier than it looks, buddy, which is why we never skip sky day. Do not look at the seam. It's working very hard, and it's shy about being watched.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Reach a new town and we send a cousin to rip a station there. Every one of them is called Rip. Our mother found a name she liked and saw no reason to stop.
after: Reach a new town and we'll send a cousin to rip a station there. Every one of them is called Rip, because our mother found a name she liked and saw no reason to stop.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: After that, you can rip between any two stations. Thank you for ripping with the Express. Please keep your elbows inside the sky.
after: After that, you can rip between any two stations whenever you like. Thank you for ripping with the Express, and please keep your elbows inside the sky.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Back for another rip, buddy? Say where and we'll tear it right open. Rips are free, same as always.
after: Back for another rip, buddy? Just say where and we'll tear it right open for you. Rips are free, same as always.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Spotting is free, buddy. Water, sadly, you'll have to bring yourself.
after: Spotting is free too, buddy. Water, I'm sorry to say, you'll have to bring yourself, because we get through all of ours.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: HNNNGH... Rip Tearson, Beefcake Rift Express, serving this exact spot. I'm a cousin; we hire entirely on relative strength.
after: HNNNGH... Rip Tearson, Beefcake Rift Express, proudly serving this exact spot. I'm one of the cousins, and I'm happy to say we hire entirely on relative strength.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: We are all very proud of one another and rarely speak.
after: We're all very proud of one another, the whole family, and we show it by rarely speaking.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Say where, buddy. We will rip it.
after: So just say where you're headed, buddy, and we'll rip it for you.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Need a rip, brother? I've held this sky since breakfast, and I'd hate to put it down with no one through it.
after: Need a rip, buddy? I've been holding this sky since breakfast, and I'd hate to put it down without anyone going through it.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Shhh. Keep it down, buddy, there's a Wrinkle asleep behind the crates. Rip Tearson, Cousin Number Seven, Rift Express. Allegedly.
after: Shhh, keep it down, buddy, there's a Wrinkle asleep behind the crates. I'm Rip Tearson, Cousin Number Seven, Rift Express. Allegedly.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: They told me this place didn't exist, so I ripped a hole to it anyway. Sometimes you just have to believe in yourself. The sauce smell helped.
after: They told me this place didn't exist, so I went ahead and ripped a hole to it anyway, because sometimes you just have to believe in yourself. The sauce smell helped a lot too.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Loosen the shoulders. Roll the neck. Tear a hole in the fabric of space. And never, ever skip leg day.
after: Loosen the shoulders, roll the neck, and tear a hole in the fabric of space. And never, ever skip leg day, brother.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: HNNNGH. Rip Tearson, Cousin Number Eight, rift technician and tree enthusiast. This is where I found the hatch, buddy, and no, I didn't open it.
after: HNNNGH. Rip Tearson, Cousin Number Eight, rift technician and tree enthusiast. This is where I found the hatch, buddy, and no, before you ask, I didn't open it.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: I have manners. Mostly.
after: I've got manners, mostly, and my mother would hear about it if I hadn't.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Say the word and I'll rip you back to {town}. Or, if you're going down the hatch, I'll hold the sky open till you're back up.
after: Say the word and I'll rip you back to {town}. Or if you're going down the hatch, I'll hold the sky open right here till you're back up.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Spotter! Big news. You know that forest outside town, where you first turned up?
after: Spotter! I've got big news. You know that forest outside town, the one where you first turned up?

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: I did not open it. I have manners, and also I am scared. But I did put a rift station up there, so you can pop over whenever you like.
after: I didn't open it, because I have manners, and also because I'm scared. But I did put a rift station up there, so you can pop over whenever you like.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: It is on the Express now. Come to any of my stations, say 'forest', and I will tear it right open.
after: It's on the Express now, so come to any of my stations and say 'forest', and I'll tear it right open for you.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Ah, a card person! I can always tell: you check your pockets for a deck before you check them for money. Dex Shufflewick, travelling cardsharp.
after: Ah, a card person! I can always tell, because you people check your pockets for a deck before you check them for money. Dex Shufflewick, travelling cardsharp, and the best you'll meet this week.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I keep a little memory table in every Path's country, dealt from that Path's own cards. Beat my score at all four, then find me for the final table.
after: I keep a little memory table in every Path's country, each one dealt from that Path's own cards. Beat my score at all four of them, and then come and find me for the final table.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Win that, and you can have my Matching Pair, the luckiest boots in the kingdom. I won them off a magician, who won them off a duck. Sit down, let's see your memory.
after: Win that, and you can have my Matching Pair, the luckiest boots in the kingdom. I won them off a magician, who won them off a duck. So sit down, friend, and let's see that memory of yours.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Back for another round? Same cards, new shuffle. My score's on the board, if you want it.
after: Back for another round? I thought you might be. It's the same cards with a brand new shuffle, and my score's up on the board whenever you feel like taking it off me.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: All four tables, beaten. I'm impressed, and slightly poorer in spirit. The final table is two cards from every Path, and I'm not going easy.
after: All four tables beaten, and I'm impressed, and a little poorer in spirit. The final table is two cards from every Path, and I'll tell you now, as a friend, that I'm not going easy.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: You cleaned me out, and the boots suit you better than they suited me. The table's still open, if you just like the game.
after: You cleaned me out, fair and square, and those boots suit you better than they ever suited me. The table's still open, mind, if you just like the game as much as I do.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Cards face down, eyes up. Watch what turns over.
after: Cards face down and eyes up, friend, and watch closely what turns over.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Hm. Lucky.
after: Now that was lucky, and I do like a lucky player.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Not bad. Not good either, but not bad.
after: Not bad at all. I've seen better, but I was the one doing it.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: You've done this before.
after: Oh, you've done this before, haven't you?

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Don't get used to it.
after: Nicely found. Now let's see you do it twice.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: The cards like you. Suspicious.
after: The cards like you, friend, and they don't like everybody.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: So close. Well. Not close.
after: Ooh, so close. Well, close-ish, between friends.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Remember where that one went.
after: Never mind, just remember where that one went.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: The cards remember. Do you?
after: The cards remember where they are, so you only have to keep up.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Nope. Try the other one.
after: Not that one, I'm afraid. Have another go.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I saw that. Did you?
after: I saw where it went. I'd tell you, but that's my living.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Well! That's my score beaten. Fair and square, sadly.
after: Well, there goes my score, beaten fair and square. I'd be upset if it hadn't been such a pleasure to watch.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Every pair found, just a few moves over. Deal again?
after: Every pair found, and only a few moves over my score. Shall I deal again?

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Out of moves. Happens to the best of us. Mostly to you.
after: That's you out of moves, I'm afraid. It happens to the best of us, and it happened to me for years before I got good.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: A well with opinions. I'm keeping the bottle anyway.
after: It says it remembers the way home, which is more than I do. I think I'll keep the bottle close.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: There is a door under the old well that has been locked since before I was born.
after: There's a door under the old well, dearie, that has been locked since before I was born, and I'll have you know that is a very long time for a door to sulk.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I always thought the key was lost, but it wasn't, dearie. Somebody hid it in a chest right here in town. Find it, and we'll see what the door is for.
after: I always thought the key was lost, but it wasn't. Somebody hid it in a chest right here in town, so if you find it for me, we'll see what that door is for.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: The key's in a hidden chest somewhere in town. Look in the odd corners, dearie; this town has never quite managed a straight one.
after: The key's in a hidden chest somewhere in town, so look in the odd corners, dearie. This town has never quite managed a straight one, and I've had a long time to check.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: You found it. Look at the bow: four little carvings in a ring. Hm. Never mind that. I'm too old for stairs, dearie, and you're not.
after: You found it! Look at the bow, with the four little carvings in a ring. Hm. Well, never mind that now. I'm far too old for stairs, dearie, and you're not, so it had better be you.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: The door's the iron hatch beside the well. Go on down. Whatever's under it belonged to the Old Kingdom, not to me, so mind the stairs.
after: The door's the iron hatch beside the well, so go on down when you're ready. Whatever's under it belonged to the Old Kingdom and not to me, dearie, so mind the stairs and mind your manners.

speaker: Shiro Swindle
before: You found me! Nobody finds me, which can only mean this is a trick. Mine, obviously.
after: You found me! But nobody ever finds me, which can only mean this is a trick, and as I'm the only trickster here, it must be one of mine. Marvellous!

speaker: Shiro Swindle
before: SMOKE BOMB!!! The oldest trick in the book. Page one. I wrote page one.
after: SMOKE BOMB!!! It's the oldest trick in the book, right there on page one, and I should know, because I wrote page one.

speaker: Shiro Swindle
before: You hit a log. A very convincing log. I gave it my eyebrows.
after: You hit a log! A very convincing log, I grant you, because I gave it my eyebrows, and I shall be wanting those back.
